result.title: Stochastic Nonlinearities Improve Uncertainty Estimation
result.comment: Accepted to the British Machine Vision Conference (BMVC) 2026. 33 pages, including supplementary material
result.summary: Reliable uncertainty estimation is important across visual recognition tasks, providing information about the confidence and reliability of model predictions. Many uncertainty estimation methods obtain predictive diversity through mechanisms that can suppress intermediate features, perturb the input, or require substantial additional computation. Stochastic activation functions, where network units randomly select between multiple nonlinearities during a forward pass, have previously been used to improve optimization behavior, mitigate limitations of fixed ReLU activations, and increase output diversity. In this work, we reframe stochastic activation switching as a lightweight mechanism for uncertainty estimation. The proposed method samples between nonlinear activation functions, inducing predictive diversity while keeping intermediate feature pathways active. This enables uncertainty estimation from a single trained model without the training cost of ensembles, task-specific uncertainty heads, or architectural redesign. We evaluate the proposed approach across classification, semantic segmentation, and out-of-distribution detection using convolutional and transformer-based architectures on diverse datasets. Across these settings, stochastic activation switching improves uncertainty quality while preserving competitive primary-task performance, showing that stochastic nonlinearities provide an effective and information-preserving source of predictive variation for visual recognition.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把「随机激活切换」（前向时随机选取不同非线性函数）重新解释为轻量级不确定性估计机制，使单模型产生预测多样性并保留中间特征通路，在分类、语义分割与 OOD 检测上验证不确定性质量提升且主任务性能不降。
AI.relevance_reason: 其信息保留式的随机性来源与置信度信号，可能为 latent 推理中的停止决策或并行采样多样性提供借鉴；但随机非线性是否真的反映状态内容的不确定性仍需核查。
